title: Objects, properties, methods
learningObjectives: Explain objects, properties, methods and process JavaScript collections correctly.

understand.concept: Objects store related data as key/value properties. Properties can be accessed using dot or bracket notation. A method is a function stored as an object property. Object literals are a common way to represent structured records such as learners, courses, and settings.
understand.whyItMatters: Objects help model real application data. Use clear property names and understand when bracket notation is needed for dynamic keys or keys that are not valid identifiers.
understand.analogy: An object is like a labelled record: each property name tells you what value is stored.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript array and object methods have defined mutation, iteration, and reference semantics.

explain.narrative: The object stores three data properties and one method. Dot and bracket notation access its values.

examples.explanation: The object stores three data properties and one method. Dot and bracket notation access its values.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the array or object values described.

practise.guidedTask: Create a learner object with name, course, progress, and a method that returns a summary string.
practise.independentTask: Build a small collection-processing example using arrays and objects. Test empty collections, missing values, and mutation behaviour.
hints: Check whether a method mutates or returns a new value.
Use clear object property names and deliberate copying.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Objects, properties, methods</title></head><body>
<script>const learner={name:'Asha',course:'HTML',completed:4,greet(){return `Hello, ${this.name}`;}};console.log(learner.name,learner['course'],learner.greet());</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: How do you access an object property using a dynamic key?
questions.explanation: Bracket notation evaluates the key expression and accesses the corresponding property.

questions.prompt: What should you check when using an array method?
options: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
Whether the array contains strings only
questions.answer: Whether it mutates the source or returns a new value
questions.explanation: Mutation behaviour matters when arrays are shared across application code.
